newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Qatar oil capacity up 100,000 bpd by end 97 - MEES.
newsitem.headline: Qatar oil capacity up 100,000 bpd by end 97 - MEES.

text.p: Qatar's oil capacity will be boosted up to 100,000 barrels per day (bpd) by the end of next year with foreign firms bringing on new fields, the Middle East Economic Survey (MEES) reported on Monday.

"MEES learns that Qatar's crude oil production capacity is slated to increase from the present level of around 500,000 bpd to 530,000 bpd by end October and to as much as 600,000 bpd by end-1997," the Cyprus-based weekly said.
"Based on present discoveries and development plans crude oil production could very well exceed the 700,000 bpd by the year 2000," it reported.
OPEC member Qatar has a quota of 398,000 bpd though actual output has been running closer to 500,000 bpd.
Atlantic Richfield (ARCO) is expected to start producing at its Al-Rayyan field in October at around 10,000 bpd, rising to some 30,000 bpd by the end of the month.
Eventual capacity at Al-Rayyan could reach 50,000 bpd around the year 2000.
France's Elf Aquitaine is set to begin output in January at its Al-Khalij block at 10,000 bpd, rising to 30,000 bpd soon afterwards, MEES reported.

In addition to work by state-owned Qatar General Petroleum Corporation (QGPC) to boost output at the onshore Dukhan field by around 100,000 bpd to 370,000 bpd by the year 2000, U.S. firms Chevron and Pennzoil are carrying out seismic work.
MEES said that QGPC was also in negotiations with two other unnamed firms to take up acreage.
Qatar oil officials have stated previously that they aim to lift Qatar's capacityy to more than 700,000 bpd by the turn of the decade.
